definitions.explanation: A state of throwing caution to the wind out of frustration or despair, acting without caring about consequences.

examples.english: I gave up and went reckless.

examples.japanese: やけくそ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{全部|ぜんぶ}→全部：02888_zenbu⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: Out of sheer desperation, I ate the whole lot.

examples.japanese: やけくそ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧しまった。
examples.english: I went on a reckless shopping spree.

examples.japanese: ⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧やけくそだ、⟦どう→どう：00543_dou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧で⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なれ→なる：01970_naru⟧。

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
やけ (desperation, also written {自棄|やけ}) plus ⟦くそ→くそ：10783_kuso⟧ (an intensifier, literally "crap").

COMMON PATTERNS:
- やけくそ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become desperate and reckless
- やけくそ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ + verb: to do something recklessly, out of frustration

SIMILAR WORDS:
- やけ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: the plain form, without the coarse ⟦くそ→くそ：10783_kuso⟧; also ⟦やけ{食|ぐ}い→やけ食い：08073_yakegui⟧ (stress eating) and ⟦やけ{酒|ざけ}→やけ酒：30996_yakezake⟧ (drinking to drown one's sorrows)
- ⟦{捨|す}て{鉢|ばち}→捨て鉢：16336_sutebachi⟧: desperate, giving up; more literary
